newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia July-Nov budget deficit A$12.49 bln.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia July-Nov budget deficit A$12.49 bln.

text.p: Australia's underlying budget deficit for the five months to November, the first five months of fiscal 1996/97, was A$12.49 billion, compared with A$10.57 billion a year earlier, Finance Minister John Fahey said on Tuesday.
The headline balance was a deficit of A$8.53 billion for the same period, compared with a A$7.29 billion deficit a year earlier, Fahey said in a statement.
The underlying measure excludes the proceeds from asset sales and state debt repayments to the federal government.
The month of November alone produced an underlying deficit of A$2.21 billion compared with A$3.28 billion in November 1995.
The monthly headline deficit was A$2.07 billion, up from A$2.91 billion.
Revenue growth to date was up 1.1 percent, compared with the budget's assumption of 7.0 percent growth.
Government spending, meanwhile, is running more strongly than budgeted. Growth to date was 3.3 percent, compared with the budget's assumption of 2.4 percent.

The rise in revenue was mainly due to gross pay as you earn (PAYE) collections, gross non-PAYE (other) individuals collections, fringe benefits tax, withholding tax, petroleum resource rent tax, and other taxes, fees and fines, he said.
The monthly figures are highly seasonal and cannot be extrapolated to estimate a final outcome for 1996/97.
Treasurer Peter Costello on Tuesday revised the government's forecast for 1996/97 underlying budget deficit to A$8.49 billion from A$5.65 billion forecast in the August budget.

"The growth in outlays compared to 1995/96 mainly reflects higher outlays on sole parent pensions, family payments, an increase in medical benefits and hospital funding grants, a one-off settlement payment made to Victoria and lower state debt repayments," Fahey said in a statement.
